name: chart
description: Numbers as a picture, with the numbers as a table under it: how many tasks were done each week, spend by month, how many of each status. From records, kept current, or from values given. Bars or a line, drawn on the server, at a glance, in brief, in full or as a page.

use.when: a person wants to see how something compares or changes: counts by category, totals over time.
use.not: one number with no comparison, which is words; or a list of the records themselves, which is a collection.
use.with: a caption saying what is counted, and a description saying what the picture shows in words.

type.description: A content type whose records are counted, such as task. Leave out to give the series yourself.

by.description: With type: the field to group by. A field with choices, a yes-or-no field, a ref (grouped by title), or a date field (grouped by period); created_at and updated_at work too.

period.description: With a date field in by: the size of each group. Defaults to month.

sum.description: With type: a number field to add up per group instead of counting records.

where.description: With type: conditions the records must meet, as a collection block takes them: done=true, project=<id>.

series.description: The values, each with a label. Filled in by the server when type is given.

kind.description: Bars compare groups; a line shows change over time.

caption.description: What is counted, as the chart's title: Tasks done each week. Filled in by the server from type, by and sum when left out.

description.description: What the picture shows, in a sentence, for whoever cannot see it: Done tasks rose from 3 to 9 over four weeks.

target.description: A value to reach, drawn as a line across the chart and named at its end; the scale makes room for it. A habit's page passes its target.

targetLabel.description: The word before the target on its line: limit for a most not to pass.

unit.description: A word or sign after each value, such as € or hours.

detail.description: glance is the last value with its trend, for a corner. brief is a small line with the last value. full is the chart with the numbers a click away. page is the chart with the table open, for when the chart has the screen to itself.

problem.description: Filled in by the server when the type, field or sum is wrong, saying what to use instead. Leave out.

summary.description: The text on the disclosure that reveals the numbers table; defaults to the caption when omitted.

a11y.role: img at full and page, with the table beside it; status at glance

keyboard.does: reaches the Numbers disclosure at full detail, which opens the table

wcag.notes: The picture is an SVG named by its caption and described by the description (1.1.1), and every value is also in a real table with headers (1.3.1), open at page detail and behind a native disclosure at full. Values are written on the bars and points, so colour never carries a number alone (1.4.1). A glance is a status with the last value and its trend in words. Nothing needs JavaScript.

machine.identify: Read data-kind for bar or line and data-record-type for the type counted. The table under the picture has one row per group: label, value.
machine.operate: Change what is counted through the block's type, by, period, sum and where props; for given numbers, series.

props.caption: Tasks done each week
props.description: Done tasks rose from 3 to 9 over four weeks, with a dip in the third.

props.caption: Spend by month
props.description: Spend was steady around 300 until August, then 480 in September.
